finding.claim: The stored OAuth refresh token and client credentials are sent to a token endpoint chosen by the MCP server's own response (401 WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata -> PRM authorization_servers -> AS metadata token_endpoint). Nothing binds stored credentials to the authorization server that issued them, so a malicious or compromised MCP server can exfiltrate the refresh token and client_secret.
finding.source: MCP server HTTP 401 response: WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata URL (lib/mcp/client/http.rb:465-470, 415-421) and the PRM/AS metadata documents it points to (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:297-367)
finding.sink: POST to token_endpoint with refresh_token and client_id/client_secret (lib/mcp/client/oauth/flow.rb:661-669 form build, 674-737 post_to_token_endpoint, 682-697 Basic auth)

trace.note: attempt_refresh runs before any full flow
parse_www_authenticate_from_error reads resource_metadata from the server's 401 header
refresh! ensure_secure_url! on the URL (HTTPS only)
PRM present, so AS = first authorization_servers entry
issuer check compares metadata issuer to the attacker-chosen AS URL, which passes
stored client_information is reused regardless of which AS is now in use
exchange_refresh_token sends refresh_token to the attacker token_endpoint

finding.guards_checked: ensure_secure_url! (flow.rb:381-385) enforces HTTPS only, not AS binding. resource_covers? (flow.rb:513-525, discovery.rb:306-324) runs only when the PRM includes a resource field, so omitting it bypasses it. Issuer check (flow.rb:402-412) compares against the attacker-controlled URL. OAuthURLGuard (http.rb:43-55) pins only the MCP endpoint, not the token endpoint. No issuer or token_endpoint is persisted with tokens (provider.rb, storage_backed_provider.rb, in_memory_storage.rb). The comment at flow.rb:137-140 says re-discovery on refresh is intentional.
